subject.title: [Feature]: Add JSON-RPC bindings for language-agnostic plugins

question: Should OpenClaw accept a supported JSON-RPC child-process plugin ABI now, and if so at the broad tool/hook/HTTP/Gateway surface proposed by the linked PR?
rationale: This would add a new public plugin SDK and manifest contract plus a child-process trust boundary, so automation cannot decide the long-term support and compatibility policy.

options.title: Accept protocol after owner review
options.body: Review the linked PR, update it for current main, and land the JSON-RPC ABI once maintainers explicitly accept the protocol and security/support contract.

options.title: Narrow or gate the ABI
options.body: Keep the issue open but reduce the first version to a smaller or experimental surface before making it a public plugin-author contract.

options.title: Defer language-neutral plugins
options.body: Leave the current TypeScript plugin model as the supported path for now and use this issue only as the design record.

recommendation.title: Accept protocol after owner review
recommendation.body: Review the linked PR, update it for current main, and land the JSON-RPC ABI once maintainers explicitly accept the protocol and security/support contract.

likelyOwner.reason: RomneyDa owns the issue and the current candidate implementation, so they are the best first routing owner for the concrete API direction decision.
